t: In front of you is the equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington, on the north side of Hyde Park Corner. The open space around it, now the middle of a large roundabout, was once called Wellington Place. Arthur Wellesley, the Duke, was a Field Marshal and statesman, a leading figure in early nineteenth century politics who served as Prime Minister. The sculptor was Joseph Edgar Boehm, an Austrian-born British artist who kept a large studio in London. He's also known for the Jubilee head of Queen Victoria on coinage.
